assumptions: USD million except counts. Hospital measures occupancy as occupied bed-days/available bed-days; inpatient and outpatient revenues separate.

qas.question: Calculate annual staffed-bed capacity.
What was inpatient occupancy?
Find net inpatient revenue per occupied bed-day.
What is the combined service contribution after shared overhead?
Why not use inpatient bed-days to divide all hospital revenue?

qas.question: Does higher occupancy establish better clinical quality?

qas.question: Can the average length of stay be found?

qas.question: Can operating return on hospital capital be computed?

assumptions: USD million and thousand tonnes. Grain contract converts wet mass to dry mass at specified moisture; payable standard mass = dry mass / .86. No spoilage other than moisture.

evidence.text: Delivered wet grain 100 thousand tonnes at 18% moisture. Standard moisture 14%; price $220 per standard tonne.
Actual purchased lot processing cost 1.2 million and storage cost .6 million, both included in analytical direct cost. Sale of whole adjusted lot at $260 per standard tonne.
No freight, interest or price-risk data. Moisture adjustment is quantity normalization, not a cash fee.

qas.question: Determine dry-matter quantity.
qas.answer: 100×.82=82 thousand tonnes.

qas.question: What standard-moisture weight is payable?
qas.answer: 82/.86≈95.3488 thousand tonnes.

qas.question: Find the purchase consideration in million USD.
Calculate analytical direct margin in dollars after processing and storage.
Why is wet delivered mass not multiplied directly by the contract price?
qas.answer: The contract pays on normalized moisture, which excludes excess water.

qas.question: Is the difference between wet and standard mass evidence of theft?
qas.answer: No. It follows the stipulated moisture normalization.

qas.question: Can the actual cash collections be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Selling price and volume are stated, not settlement timing.

qas.question: Can we establish total farm profitability from this lot?
qas.answer: No. Farming costs and other lots are absent.

assumptions: USD million. Toy endowment rules: donor-restricted corpus may not be spent; annual distribution is 4% of trailing average NAV, subject to cash available. No other flows.

evidence.text: Donor-restricted corpus 300. Trailing three-year NAV values 320, 350, 380. Current NAV before distribution 390.
Cash available for approved educational spending 16; distribution policy 4% of average of the three values.
Separate unrestricted operating cash 20 is outside endowment. No donor permission to invade corpus.

qas.question: Find the trailing average NAV.
What annual endowment distribution is allowed?
qas.answer: 350×4%=14 million, below available cash 16.

qas.question: How much approved spending cash remains after distribution?
qas.answer: 16−14=2 million USD.

qas.question: Determine endowment NAV after distribution assuming no other change.
qas.answer: 390−14=376 million USD.

qas.question: Why not use 390 as the spending-rate base?
qas.answer: The policy explicitly uses trailing average NAV, not current NAV.

qas.question: Does the 300 corpus count as unrestricted operating liquidity?
qas.answer: No. Donor restrictions prohibit invading corpus under the case.

qas.question: Can next year's distribution be forecast exactly?
qas.answer: No. Future NAV and available spending cash are not known.

qas.question: Can the university's consolidated surplus be determined?
qas.answer: No. Tuition, operating costs and other resources are absent.

assumptions: USD million. Toy content amortization uses actual viewing fraction of estimated lifetime viewing. No impairment or estimate revision in base. Production paid at start; revenue separate.

evidence.text: A series costs 90, expected lifetime views 30 million; 12 million views occur in year one.
Year-one subscription revenue attributable to series 55; incremental distribution cost 8.
An alternative estimate of lifetime views is 24 million, applied as a same-date sensitivity, not additional expense.

qas.question: Calculate base content amortization in year one.
qas.answer: 90×12/30=36 million USD.

qas.question: Determine remaining content carrying amount under base.
qas.answer: 90−36=54 million USD.

qas.question: Find the contribution after base amortization and distribution cost.
qas.answer: 55−36−8=11 million USD.

qas.question: How much greater is amortization under the alternative estimate?
qas.answer: 90×12/24−36=9 million USD.

qas.question: Why not expense the full production cash outlay again in the contribution?
qas.answer: Production is capitalized in the toy policy; the current cost is amortization, not both outlay and amortization.

qas.question: Should sensitivity expense be added to base expense?
qas.answer: No. It is an alternative measurement of the same asset and period.

qas.question: Can content profitability over its entire life be established?
qas.answer: No. Future revenue, viewing and costs are missing.

qas.question: Can exact subscriber acquisitions attributable to the series be determined?
qas.answer: No. Viewing count is not a new-subscriber attribution metric.

assumptions: USD million. All shipment sales recognized before rebates; rebates and chargebacks reduce revenue. No returns. Opening rebate payable and settlements supplied; cost of sales separate.

evidence.text: Gross shipment sales 800; estimated wholesaler chargebacks 90, payer rebates 140, discounts 30.
Opening rebate/chargeback payable 100; current rebate and chargeback accrual 230; cash settled 180. Discounts granted at invoice, not payable.
Cost of sales 180; R&D 120; selling costs 100. Other income and tax absent.

qas.question: Calculate total gross-to-net sales deductions.
qas.answer: 90+140+30=260 million USD.

qas.question: Determine net recognized sales.
qas.answer: 800−260=540 million USD.

qas.question: Find closing rebate and chargeback payable.
Compute operating subtotal after disclosed cost items.
Why is cash rebate settlement not the same as current gross-to-net deductions?
qas.answer: Settlements include liabilities from different periods; accruals measure current consideration reductions.

qas.question: Would subtracting the cash settlement again from net sales be appropriate?
qas.answer: No. It reduces the payable; the related deductions are already included in net sales.

qas.question: Can actual net price per prescription be found?
qas.answer: No. Prescription volume and product mix are missing.

qas.question: Can the drug's patent-expiry impact be quantified?
qas.answer: No. Patent dates, competition and future pricing are not supplied.

assumptions: USD million. Toy prepaid mobile credit: revenue recognized when service used or credit legally expires; no estimated breakage in advance. No other movements.

evidence.text: Opening prepaid balance 18; new top-ups collected 72. Customers consume 65 of credit during year.
Unused credit of 4 expires during year under contract; no refunds.
Network service cost 28 for consumed service. No other expense, usage units or subscriber count.

qas.question: What total prepaid credit became available during the year?
qas.answer: 18+72=90 million USD.

qas.question: Find total recognized prepaid revenue.
qas.answer: 65+4=69 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate the closing prepaid obligation.
qas.answer: 90−65−4=21 million USD.

qas.question: Determine gross profit under the stated service cost scope.
qas.answer: 69−28=41 million USD.

qas.question: Why is top-up cash not immediately revenue?
qas.answer: The operator still owes service until usage or qualifying expiration.

qas.question: Does expired credit imply another cash collection at expiry?
qas.answer: No. Cash was collected earlier; expiry releases the obligation.

qas.question: Can prepaid ARPU be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Active subscriber count is missing.

qas.question: Can next year's breakage be forecast from 4 alone?
qas.answer: No. Credit cohorts, expiry patterns and future behavior are unknown.

assumptions: USD million. Toy royalty: 4% on first 100 revenue, 7% on excess; apply marginal tiers, not flat. Production and sales all in year, no other royalty.

evidence.text: Copper concentrate revenue 180; deductible operating cost 100, but royalty base is gross sales.

qas.question: Calculate royalty on the first tier.
qas.answer: 100×4%=4 million USD.

qas.question: What royalty applies to the excess 80?
qas.answer: 80×7%=5.6 million USD.

qas.question: Determine total base royalty.

qas.question: Find stress operating surplus after royalty.

qas.question: Can the after-tax cash return be calculated?
